name: Exampleland
currency_note: Exampleland uses the example crown; the app shows US dollars.

tax_year.return_due: File the return online by 31 January after the tax year ends.

summary: Made-up content for tests and screenshots: none of this is a real country's rules. Exampleland taxes profits when you sell and dividends you receive, with a yearly tax-free amount for each. Savings accounts called Example Savers are free of tax.

topics.title: Profit when you sell
points: Profit on shares and funds is taxed in the year you sell.
Shares held for more than three years are taxed at a lower rate (the long-hold rate, langhold).

topics.title: Dividends
points: Your broker takes 15% when the dividend is paid. You settle the rest in your return.

topics.title: Interest on savings
points: Interest is added to your other income and taxed at your income tax rate.

topics.title: Tax-free amounts
points: Each year the first part of your profit and of your dividends is tax-free. An unused amount cannot be carried to the next year.

topics.title: Tax-free and tax-deferred accounts
points: An Example Saver account is free of tax on interest, dividends and profit.

topics.title: Losses
points: A loss is first set against profit of the same year; the rest is carried forward without a time limit.
Buying the same shares back within 30 days of the sale cancels the loss for tax.

topics.title: Foreign shares
points: Tax taken abroad is credited up to the Exampleland tax on the same dividend.

topics.title: What your broker does and what you do
points: A local broker sends the tax office a yearly statement of your sales and dividends.
With a foreign broker you report every sale yourself.

dates.what: Last day to file the return for the tax year before.
Last day of the tax year: the tax-free amounts of this year end.

upcoming: The tax-free profit falls to $2,000 from 6 April 2027 (announced, not yet law).

unverified.point: Some banks say the Example Saver limit will rise in 2028.
